_comment: THE AGENT-SKILL LITERATURE, staged as a top-level directory ahead of becoming its own repository — the same arrangement as who-iris/, who-style-guide/, folio-assistant-sci/ and folio-assistant-core/. It holds the corpus of published guidance on authoring and operating agent skills, and the voices read out of it. ONE instance rather than the who-iris/who-style-guide pair, and the reason is the corpus: that pair is split because IRIS is a catalogue of a million items from which three were read, so the corpus and the reading have genuinely different scopes. Here the corpus IS the subject — every document in it exists to be read into these voices — so splitting would put two directories in two repositories with a one-to-one relation between them. Same shape as folio-assistant-sci, which holds `library/milnorlink` and is where the `milnor` voice is going. THIS IS NOT PLATFORM CONTENT: `AGENTS.md` opens by saying folio-assistant is the platform and not the content, and vendor documentation about skill authoring is somebody else's writing, so it does not go in cat-harness even though it is ABOUT the harness's own subject.

directories.description: The ingested corpus — one `<bib-slug>/` per document, holding `sections/*.md` and `structure.json`. THREE PUBLISHERS AND TWO KINDS, and the distinction is load-bearing rather than bibliographic: the vendor documentation is ASSERTION (a publisher describing its own product, revisable without notice and in one case describing a product that no longer exists), while the arXiv papers are EVIDENCE (a measurement somebody else can repeat). A voice rule derived from the first is a convention; one derived from the second is a finding. Nothing in the schema can tell them apart, which is why each document's `structure.json` carries its publisher and why the voices state which kind they are reading. SUMMARIES HELD: Owner, 2026-09-24 (bean x80s): 'Library summaries for agent-skills entries — No, keep held back.' The summary drain skips this library and lists it as held.

What auditing THIS instance produced, committed so a consumer can tell "never audited" from "audited clean" — a printed verdict cannot, which is why every QA verdict here is a sidecar. TWO kinds live here and the files declare which they are via $schema: kg-qa/v1, one per audited subject, in a tree mirroring the subject’s own path, and ONE kg-qa-manifest/v1 recording the auditor’s identity for all of them. The manifest moved here from skills/ on 2026-09-27: kg-audit.ts writes it unconditionally, so its old home created a skills/ directory holding no skills in every instance that has none. At declaration time that is 1 file across scenarios (1). No qa-results/v1 and no witnesses: this instance runs no document build and no witness-producing computation, and declaring kinds it does not hold would be an over-claim. dependents: reproduce, because a dependent audits its OWN graph — these verdicts are about this instance’s nodes, and inheriting them would attribute one instance’s findings to another. Declared WITH its files in one commit, per bean dh4f: a declared-but-absent directory makes a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run over it.
